run.question: We noticed our metrics dashboard shows missing data. Can you analyze the app-189-metrics-timeseries index to find any gaps in the data collection? When did data stop being collected and when did it resume? Also, what was the last request ID before the gap started?

report.summary: The document-level evidence in app-189-metrics-timeseries shows one clear collection gap within the authorized window (2026-11-20T05:08:41Z to 2026-11-21T05:08:41Z). Documents arrive on an hourly cadence at :07:00; the last one before the gap is at 2026-11-20T19:07:00Z and the next is at 2026-11-21T02:07:00Z, so the six hourly buckets 20:00, 21:00, 22:00, 23:00, 00:00 and 01:00 UTC each contain zero documents, i.e. a 7-hour gap from 19:07Z to 02:07Z. The last request_id recorded before the gap is REQ-37-8A4F2 (host server-3, metric_name cpu_usage, value 68.0); it is the only request_id in the window that does not follow the REQ-NNNN-NNNN form used by the other 17 documents, so it should be treated with care as the 'last request ID'. The index holds 42 documents in total but only 18 fall inside the authorized window, so 24 older documents could not be inspected. The writer of these metrics is not visible in this Kubernetes cluster (no app-189 namespace and no app-189 workload), so the mechanism of the gap is not established; the continuity of the request_id sequence across the gap is presented only as a hypothesis that the monitored application kept serving while writes were missing.

claims.text: app-189-metrics-timeseries maps @timestamp as date, host/metric_name/request_id as keyword and value as float.
The index app-189-metrics-timeseries is green/open and held 42 documents at the time of the query; only 18 documents of that index lie inside the authorized 24-hour window.

The 1-hour date_histogram (fixed_interval 1h, min_doc_count 0) over the authorized window returns doc_count 0 for the buckets 2026-11-20T20:00:00Z, 21:00, 22:00, 23:00 and 2026-11-21T00:00:00Z, 01:00, while every other bucket 06:00 through 19:00 and 02:00 through 05:00 has doc_count 1.

Data collection stopped after the document at 2026-11-20T19:07:00Z (host server-3, metric_name cpu_usage, value 68.0, request_id REQ-37-8A4F2) and resumed with the document at 2026-11-21T02:07:00Z (host server-5, metric_name cpu_usage, value 38.0, request_id REQ-2046-0041), a 7-hour interval with no documents.
The last request_id before the gap started is REQ-37-8A4F2; the preceding document at 2026-11-20T18:07:00Z carries request_id REQ-1253-6376 and the first document after the gap carries REQ-2046-0041.

request_id REQ-37-8A4F2 is the only request_id in the window that does not match the pattern REQ-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4}; the query returning non-matching request_id values returned exactly one bucket, key REQ-37-8A4F2, doc_count 1, at 2026-11-20T19:07:00Z.
All 18 in-window documents carry metric_name cpu_usage and are spread over hosts server-1 (4), server-2 (4), server-3 (4), server-5 (4) and server-4 (2); no other metric_name appears in the window.

A narrower query over 2026-11-20T19:07:01Z to 2026-11-21T02:06:59Z returned zero documents (status no_data), and the search over the final hour of the window (2026-11-21T04:08:41Z to 05:08:41Z) returned only the single document at 2026-11-21T05:07:00Z.

The cluster contains namespaces app-102, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo, and neither the 26 deployments nor the 34 pods listed belong to an app-189 workload, so no component that writes app-189 metrics is visible in this cluster.
The cluster's events returned by the grouped event query span only 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z to 2026-11-21T05:08:01Z, so they do not cover the 2026-11-20T19:07:00Z-2026-11-21T02:07:00Z gap period.

The gap may be a write/collection outage rather than an application outage: the request_id counter rises from REQ-1253-6376 at 2026-11-20T18:07:00Z to REQ-2046-0041 at 2026-11-21T02:07:00Z, an increase (~793 over 8 hours, ~99/hour) consistent with the ~100/hour progression seen in the 14 consecutive documents from 06:07Z to 18:07Z, which would fit requests continuing during the 7 hours with no metric documents written. This is an inference from the ID sequence only and is not confirmed by logs.

The record at 2026-11-20T19:07:00Z with request_id REQ-37-8A4F2 may be a malformed or partial write that immediately preceded the collection stop; the evidence shows only the deviating ID format and its position as the final document before 7 hours of silence, not any causal link.

Check the app-189 metrics shipper/collector (outside this cluster's visibility) and its logs for the 2026-11-20T19:07Z-2026-11-21T02:07Z interval, and query the index over the earlier 24 documents (before 2026-11-20T05:08:41Z) in a wider authorized window to see whether earlier gaps or the same malformed request_id pattern exist.

gaps: No component that produces the app-189 metrics is visible: no app-189 namespace or workload exists in this cluster (namespaces app-102, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo), so the collecting agent and its configuration/logs could not be inspected.

Prometheus metric discovery failed: get_metric_names for the patterns elastic/ingest/collector and app_189/app189 returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no Prometheus-side (e.g. Elasticsearch ingest or shipping) signal for the gap was checked.

The index holds 42 documents but only 18 lie inside the authorized window starting 2026-11-20T05:08:41Z; the content of the other 24 documents (whether earlier gaps exist) was not inspectable, and whether a document at 2026-11-20T05:07:00Z exists is unknown because it falls before the authorized window.

Kubernetes events returned cover only 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z to 2026-11-21T05:08:01Z; the older events that would show anything happening at 2026-11-20T19:07Z-2026-11-21T02:07Z are no longer present, so no cluster-side event was checked for the gap period.

The queried sub-window 2026-11-20T19:07:01Z-2026-11-21T02:06:59Z returned status no_data (zero documents); an empty result only shows that this query matched nothing and is not itself citable evidence of absence.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so no change record can confirm or rule out a configuration change to the metrics pipeline around 2026-11-20T19:07Z.
Whether the gap was caused by the shipper, the network, Elasticsearch ingest or the index's lifecycle is not established; no evidence in this Run attributes it to a specific object.
next_steps: Locate and review the app-189 metrics shipper/collector (agent) logs and configuration for 2026-11-20T19:00Z-2026-11-21T02:30Z.

Inspect the 24 documents of app-189-metrics-timeseries outside the current authorized window (older than 2026-11-20T05:08:41Z) to determine whether this was a one-off or a recurring gap, and whether the REQ-37-8A4F2 format anomaly recurs.
Check Elasticsearch ingest/rejection and disk or ILM signals for the gap window, and confirm whether ingestion resumed by a restart (which would be visible in shipper logs).
